item.title: Malcolm Webster Staged Car Crashes for Insurance Money
item.description: Malcolm Webster murdered his first wife, Claire Morris, in a staged crash in Scotland in 1994. Five years later, he tried to kill his second wife, Felicity Drumm, in New Zealand. Both attacks formed part of insurance schemes that led to his conviction and life sentence in 2011.

item.title: Brenda Delgado Hired a Killer to Target Kendra Hatcher
item.description: Dallas dentist Kendra Hatcher was killed in 2015 in a murder plot arranged by Brenda Delgado, her boyfriend’s former partner. The investigation traced the planned attack to Delgado, who fled to Mexico before her arrest and eventual conviction for capital murder.

item.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard and the Abuse Behind the Murder
item.description: Years of abuse and fabricated illnesses preceded Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s role in the 2015 murder of her mother, Dee Dee. This overview examines the plot with Nicholas Godejohn, Gypsy’s guilty plea to second-degree murder and the abuse prosecutors considered in her sentencing.

item.title: Raoul Moat and the Seven Day Police Manhunt
item.description: In July 2010, Raoul Moat killed Chris Brown, wounded his former partner Samantha Stobbart and shot police officer David Rathband, leaving him blind. The attacks triggered a major manhunt across northeast England that ended in a standoff in Rothbury.

item.title: Christa Pike Was Sentenced to Death at 20
item.description: Description: Christa Pike was 18 when she murdered fellow Job Corps student Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville in 1995. Convicted the following year, she received a death sentence at 20, making her one of the youngest women sentenced to death in modern US history.

item.title: Barbara Opel Recruited Her Daughter Into a Murder Plot
item.description: Barbara Opel promised money and gifts to five teenagers, including her 13-year-old daughter, to kill her employer Jerry Heimann in Washington in 2001. Convicted of aggravated first-degree murder in 2003, she was sentenced to life without parole.
